brief: Tech CDS spreads have returned to recent highs and bond volatility (the MOVE index) has surged, both warning signs, but NDX and SPX are not selling off, unlike NDX's reaction to widening CDS spreads back in July. The note argues price is still the final arbiter. SPX's resilience against the MOVE surge can persist if higher yields reflect stronger growth, but becomes harder to sustain if bond market stress starts forcing broader risk reduction. Framing the setup as a cork bobbing in water, the note asks what happens if NDX takes out its range highs, arguing there is only vacuum above, meaning no technical resistance to further upside. With NDX seasonality starting now and volatility reset lower, the note argues playing a possible upside breakout via call spreads looks attractive, favoring short-dated structures because it suspects a breakout would be violent. It cites the QQQ October 750/780 call spread as offering up to 4x maximum payout.
